MKT-01-A.conclusion: Partly supported. Singapore teachers spend 6.4 h/week on marking (OECD TALIS 2024, MKT-E020), and studies elsewhere show diagnosing maths misconceptions is demanding (MKT-E022–E024). No evidence specific to tutors or tuition centres.

MKT-01-D.conclusion: Not established. MOE publishes student counts (237,966 primary students in 2024, MKT-E006) but no count of tuition centres, and MOE does not track the industry's size. Market size must remain an explicit assumption.

MKT-02-A.action_reason: Set by Hansle 2026-11-04: reviewed counter-evidence shows competitors already identify and report learning gaps.

MKT-02-B.conclusion: Synthetic by design: MathBridge's features are fictional (SYN-02). Against the Competitor Matrix, its distinguishing features are tutor review, response-level evidence links and a centre licence.

MKT-02-C.conclusion: Indirectly supported. Expert human feedback is more nuanced than AI alone (MKT-E036) and explained diagnostic results help teachers plan better (MKT-E039). No evidence that tuition centres value or would pay for these features.
